added.name: Avout
added.long_description:
Avout provides non-dilutive financing to companies building in the physical world: robotics, space, drones, autonomy, and AI infrastructure & data.

Hardware companies need capital for equipment, inventory, and production long before revenue catches up. Today they fund it with venture equity, the most expensive money they'll ever raise, because banks don't understand the assets or move at startup speed.

We're starting with asset-backed lending and revenue-based financing, using a company's own operating data to make decisions quickly. Our vision is to become the financial rails for the machine economy.

We've done this before with real assets. Artem Milinchuk founded FarmTogether (YC W'18 accepted), a farmland investment platform he scaled to $220M in assets across 50 farms, and previously invested at Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and was CFO at Full Harvest. Cofounder Cody DeVilliers built banking and payments infrastructure at Interac, Moneris, and TD Bank.
added.one_liner: Avout - new finance company for the American frontier

added.name: Luminary
added.long_description:
Luminary is an AI CEO that leads human and agent teams on company-wide missions. We're building the complete infrastructure for a fully AI-native company, starting with a world model of how your business works and building up to an AI CEO that can lead it.

Today's AI tools are good at automating the work they're handed, but they still wait to be told what to do next. So even with the abundance of AI agents, companies are still bottlenecked by leadership and vision. Someone has to decide what's worth building, rally the right people behind it, and bring it to market.

Luminary takes on that job. Instead of asking it to build a feature, you hand it part of your business to grow. It then proactively discovers opportunities, plans high-impact missions, and leads your people and its own agent swarms to accomplish them. 

Some examples of audacious missions it can execute:

- Launch a product: It spots customers building the same workaround, makes the business case, directs coding agents to build it, and rolls it out.
- Enter a new market: It finds an unexpected group of buyers, reworks positioning and pricing around them, and wins the first accounts.
- Rescue a stalled deal: It notices an enterprise deal losing momentum, designs a new strategy with your sales team, and gets it signed.

Under the hood, Luminary builds a living world model and follows a leadership constitution that shapes every call. Proprietary evals check every deliverable, and a recursive self-improvement loop turns each mission into institutional wisdom.
added.one_liner: AI CEO that leads human & agent teams on company-wide missions

long_description.before:
We make running services on Kubernetes as easy as Heroku, but on your cloud and with all the flexibility and power of Kubernetes. Companies use Skyhook so that they don't have to hire dedicated infrastructure engineers.

Although 50-70% of organizations have already adopted Kubernetes, most developers agree that it is too complex and difficult to manage. It is intended to be extremely flexible in order to solve pretty much everyone’s needs, but it can take a ton of work and many auxiliary tools to get there.

As companies grow, they spend a lot on DevOps or Platform Engineers that try to reduce the burden on developers by gluing together all the 3p tools via custom internal tools.

We are building an “internal developer platform” out of the box, with best practices and golden paths for building and operating services on Kubernetes.

We do the research on the latest and greatest tools in the extremely vibrant ecosystem, and automatically integrate for you the tools you want to use.

We operate on our customers code and in your Cloud environment, so they never locked in and never restricted, as is common with classic PaaS offerings.

If you prefer a fully hosted environment like Heroku, Fly or Vercel, we’ll host a cluster for you and offer you a one-click migration to your own cluster when you want.
long_description.after:
Radar is the missing open-source Kubernetes interface for humans and agents.

Kubernetes is easy to query, but hard to understand. Radar shows what's failing in a cluster, why, and what changed: issues and root cause, topology, an event and change timeline, Helm, GitOps (Argo CD and Flux), traffic, image internals, audits, upgrade impact and CVEs. Engineers get a UI. AI agents get a built-in MCP server with structured cluster context instead of raw YAML, and Radar can run AI investigations through the agent CLI you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode).

Radar is and always will be open source: a single Apache 2.0 binary that runs on your laptop against your kubeconfig, or in-cluster via Helm, with no agents or CRDs to install. 4.2k+ GitHub stars.

Radar Cloud keeps watching when you close the laptop: grouped alerts to Slack, AI investigations with evidence on alerts or on demand, fleet-wide issues, search and diffs across every cluster behind one MCP endpoint, 30 days of history, and shared views scoped by Kubernetes RBAC. SOC 2 on every plan; SSO, SCIM and self-managed on Enterprise.

Radar is built by Skyhook. Get started at https://radarhq.io or https://github.com/skyhook-io/radar

one_liner.before: PaaS-like experience with the power of Kubernetes, on your cloud
one_liner.after: Radar: the missing Kubernetes interface for humans and agents

long_description.before:
TensorTest (formerly Ritivel) builds evaluations, reinforcement-learning environments, and expert training data for AI labs developing creative agents, starting with video editing.

An agent can produce a valid video file without delivering an edit that meets the client’s brief. Labs need reliable ways to measure creative quality, identify failures, and give agents feedback they can learn from.

Our first benchmark, TimelineBench, gives agents client video-editing jobs with raw footage, audio, and a brief. It evaluates the finished work using a verifier calibrated on thousands of blind judgments from professional editors. Across 16 agents we tested, the best passed only 26.8% of jobs. Most failures came down to creative craft rather than broken output.

We offer labs private evaluations to identify where their models fail, training environments that use our verifier’s scores as rewards, and expert-created training data, including professional editing demonstrations, preference pairs, and grading rubrics. These offerings connect evaluation to training: identify what an agent gets wrong, provide feedback on its attempts, and supply examples of better work.

Our team comes from IIT Bombay and has trained language models and built agentic systems at Microsoft Research.
long_description.after:
TensorTest works with AI labs, robotics companies, and enterprises across the stack, from pre-training and post-training data to reinforcement learning (RL) environments and evaluations.

We scope and run custom datasets, production traces, environments, and evaluation suites, and staff domain experts onto client teams.

TimelineBench and CharacterBench are examples of our published evaluation work.

one_liner.after: AI training data, evals, and RL environments

TrueMile is a trucking company run by AI agents.  Owner-operators lease onto us and our agents find their loads, book them, make the check calls, and handle billing, paperwork, safety and compliance. They earn 30% more profit and get 7 hours a week back.

On their own, they're too small for shipper contracts, so they live on load boards, booking one load at a time. That's the trap. A load that looks great can strand you in a market with nothing coming back. 500 miles at $3.90 beats 200 at $4.10, but only if you can see the whole week. A person calls 3 to 5 brokers before human fatigue kicks in. Our AI works brokers in 10 markets at once and chains loads that connect. 

Trucking never grew on capital alone. Every new truck needed another person in the office. We do that work with software. One person can now manage 9x as many trucks.

Founder Harpreet Dhaliwal took over his family's failing fleet at 19 and has generated over $7.2M in trucking revenue. He built the system that became TrueMile.

For owner-operators and freight partnerships: harpreet@truemile.ai
long_description.after:

A job that looks great can strand you in a city where the next jobs pay less. Our AI negotiates brokers across 10 markets at once to weigh profit across the whole week, not just one job at a time.

Trucking is insanely hard to scale because more trucks always meant hiring more people. Now we're finally able to scale truck count without spending time, resources, and dollars hiring for the back-office.

long_description.before:
Dualizer builds AI-powered, physics-based process simulation and digital twins to design and scale chemical processes and optimize existing plants. We help engineering teams identify bottlenecks, increase yield and throughput, and reduce energy and production costs—improving plant efficiency and profitability.

The platform combines AI reasoning, our proprietary deterministic simulation and optimization engine, and physics-informed machine learning. Engineers can build, calibrate, and refine models through conversation, starting from a diagram, available data, or an engineering objective. Calculations account for thermodynamics, material and energy balances, equipment behavior, and operating constraints, enabling teams to optimize interconnected equipment and operating conditions across a plant.

Equipment sizing and costing, 3D layout planning, and techno-economic analysis connect process improvements to plant-level decisions. Teams can accelerate new process scale-up, debottleneck operating plants, and continually refine operating strategies as production targets and plant conditions change. Dualizer makes rigorous simulation and optimization an ongoing capability for improving industrial productivity and profitability throughout a plant’s life.
long_description.after:
Dualizer (YC F26) builds agentic physics simulation to debottleneck manufacturing—from everyday essentials like food, beverages, and medicine to the fuels and advanced materials powering aviation and modern computing.

High manufacturing costs and production bottlenecks can raise prices and cause shortages of essential goods. Inefficient production can waste resources and pollute the environment for decades. Design or operating failures can cause deadly incidents. Yet the engineering needed to design better processes and improve existing plants remains slow, manual, and highly specialized.

Dualizer’s software platform lets engineers build physics-based digital twins, design safer processes, and optimize plant performance—boosting throughput while reducing energy use and production costs.

Its ambition is to become the engineering foundation for the world’s process industries—helping startups and global manufacturers alike commercialize breakthroughs faster and make essential goods cheaper and more abundant.

Same school. Same year. Same major. David Kim, Chris Donahue, and Nathan Liu met at UC Berkeley, Class of ‘27, Chemical Engineering. Their research and industry experience in process modeling, physics-based simulation, and AI/ML gave them the foundation for a shared ambition: transforming how industrial plants are designed and operated. long_description.before:
Sutrix turns messy data from EHRs, clinical notes, wearables, and surveys into clean, study-ready datasets allowing healthcare research teams to deliver tailored patient care faster.

Before a clinical study can start, research staff spend weeks pulling patient data from disconnected systems like the EHR, REDCap, and wearable platforms, reading notes chart by chart, and reconciling conflicting entries in spreadsheets. Sutrix automates that work by deploying AI systems within each team’s own environment, linking patient records across sources, applying the study's rules, and flagging unclear cases for staff to review.

Paying research teams at 10+ institutions cut data prep by 80% going from months per study to weeks.

We're brothers who've built together for 4 years. We first solved this problem doing forward-deployed work at HSS, where we built an injury surveillance system now used by 700+ teams. Ritvik's clinical research at HSS and Emory showed us every research team has the same bottleneck. Supratik previously founded and exited an ai security company backed by a16z Speedrun, and built production AI agents at Amazon.
long_description.after:
Large health systems already earn revenue licensing de-identified clinical data to pharma. Most providers can't, because their data is scattered across EHRs, clinical notes, wearables and surveys, and they don't have the team to make it usable.

Sutrix does the work for them. We deploy inside the provider's own environment, pull records from every source, link and reconcile them, de-identify them, and package research-ready datasets for pharma and AI labs.

Our engine already runs for paying research teams and we are now expanding into health systems.

long_description.before:
Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Engineers don't have time to continually improve the agents they've shipped — the context bloat, overly chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, quietly hurting agent efficiency. With Papaya they connect their agent directly via SDK, get actionable recommendations on how to improve quality, latency, and cost, and the ones they approve are pushed to production as pull requests.

Papaya runs 200+ research-backed analyses across context, prompts, prompt caching, subagents, and tool calls. Every recommendation is ranked by impact and comes with the production runs that produced it — typically a 20%+ quality improvement on the first workflow analysis.
long_description.after:
Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Engineers don’t have time to keep improving the agents they’ve shipped. Context bloat, chatty subagents, and broken tool calls sit in production traces nobody reads, so no one can tell whether the agent is delivering the outcome it was built for.

Papaya analyzes production traces and code, groups runs by business use case, and measures each one against its intended business outcome. Over 200 research-backed analyses find what’s holding the agent back. Every fix is ranked by impact on quality, latency, and cost, and the ones engineers approve ship as pull requests. Customers typically see a 20%+ quality improvement from the first analysis.
